quote: 개발 집합 C2 −3 dB 에서 paired BLER 차이 |Δ| > 0.010 (n=640, 26 블록 이상)
title: H0 rejection rule is self-contradictory, below noise, and names no pair
consequence: 0.010 × 640 = 6.4 blocks, not 26 (26 = 0.010 × 2560, the test-set n). Measured seed-to-seed discordance of V1 on the same trials is 0.035–0.041 (raw_B1e4 vs s2/s3, C2 −3 dB); at that rate P(|Δ̂| > 0.010 | true Δ = 0, n=640) ≈ 0.14–0.20, and the McNemar MDD at n=640 is ≈0.019–0.021. So the rule 'rejects' H0 by chance one time in five for identical models, or never if '26 blocks' (Δ ≥ 0.041, twice the seed effect) is meant. §2.5 also compares three arms (기존 last-EMA, 재학습 last, 재학습 best) without saying which pair Δ refers to; 기존-vs-재학습 includes GPU nondeterminism and is a different null.
fix: State the rule as a test, not a point estimate: Δ = 재학습 best − 재학습 last on the same 640 trials, exact McNemar two-sided p < 0.05 AND |Δ| ≥ MDD (≈0.02, ≥13 blocks); report 기존-vs-재학습 as the seed/nondeterminism reference only. Delete '26 블록'.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on the document, the raw data, and the rules.

1. Self-contradictory rule (NEXT_EXPERIMENTS.md:34): "개발 집합 C2 −3 dB 에서 paired BLER 차이 |Δ| > 0.010 (n=640, 26 블록 이상)". 0.010 × 640 = 6.4 blocks; 26 blocks is 0.0406 at n=640 (or 0.010 × 2560, the test-set n from line 14). "26" appears nowhere in REVIEW_AUDIT.md, CHANGELOG_REVIEW.md or the handoff, so it is the document's own number. Any outcome between 7 and 25 discordant-net blocks is "reject" by the fraction and "accept" by the block count. Line 3 freezes §2 thresholds after commit, so this ambiguity cannot be resolved later without a DECISIONS entry — exactly what a pre-registration is supposed to prevent. Line 147's prediction "H0 채택(|Δ| < 0.01)" inherits the same ambiguity.

2. Below noise (verified, CPU-only): V1 (M-ours-dscore-C-V1) at C2 −3 dB on the identical 2560 trials, raw_B1e4 (ckpt a1) vs raw_B1e4s2 (a2) vs raw_B1e4s3 (a3): discordance 0.0355 / 0.0391 / 0.0410 (GMM b* arm: 0.0000, so the trials are truly paired). Under Δ=0 with that discordance, P(|b−c| ≥ 7 at n=640) = 0.12–0.20; exact two-sided McNemar MDD at n=640 = 0.0156–0.0187 (10–12 blocks), i.e. above the 0.010 threshold. P(|b−c| ≥ 26 | Δ=0) ≈ 1e-6–1e-8, so the "26 블록" reading essentially never rejects. The claim's MDD figure (0.019–0.021) is slightly higher than my exact computation but the conclusion is the same either way.

3. Pair not named (line 77): "{기존 last-EMA, 재학습 last, 재학습 best} 를 paired 비교" — three arms, no statement of which pair Δ in H0 refers to. score.py load_model (line 1025) always loads st["ema"], so 재학습 last = last-EMA and 재학습 best = best-EMA; both "재학습 best − 재학습 last" and "기존 last-EMA − 재학습 best" literally match H0's wording "best-epoch 가중치와 last-EMA 가중치". Line 76 itself concedes the retrain is not bit-identical (GPU nondeterminism), so the 기존-vs-재학습 pair carries a different-trajectory null for which the seed-to-seed discordance above is the correct proxy — and under that null the 6.4-block rule false-rejects ~1 in 5–8.

4. Conflict with house rules: 10_SPEC_stageC.md:150 and :256 "양측 부호검정 + 3점 규칙. 사후에 검정을 바꾸지 않는다"; :820 A3 "점추정만으로 비를 말하지 않는다"; 08_SPEC_analysis.md §2 requires a paired sign test with a power guard (≥6 discordant pairs, else UNDECIDED), implemented in Demo/exp_0925_analysis.py (MIN_DISC=6). The document's own A1 rule (line 99) uses "McNemar p < 0.05", but H0 (line 34) is a bare point-estimate threshold with no test and no power guard. H0 is also the control arm for A1 (line 78), so an unsound H0 verdict propagates into the ablation judgement.

Not a matter of taste: the rule is numerically unfollowable for a wide band of plausible outcomes, its resolvable readings are either noise-level or unrejectable, and it contradicts the frozen house test. The proposed fix (name the pair as 재학습 best − 재학습 last on the same 640 trials, exact McNemar p<0.05 plus |Δ| ≥ MDD, report 기존-vs-재학습 as the nondeterminism reference, delete "26 블록") is consistent with the cited rules.

quote: 판정: 3 attempt 중 2 이상에서 aug 의 개발 BLER 이 ctrl 보다 낮고, 6개 paired 차이를 합친 McNemar p < 0.05.
title: Pooled McNemar over attempts reuses the same 640 trials as if independent; '6개' is undefined
consequence: The three attempts are evaluated on the identical 640 (H, u, perm, noise) realisations, so the per-attempt paired differences are positively correlated through the trial (hard blocks fail under every seed). Pooling them as 3×640 (or 6×640) discordant pairs inflates the effective n and the nominal p; the true MDD stays at the n=640 level (≈0.02–0.03 at disc 0.03–0.08, i.e. a 14–22% relative reduction from BLER 0.145), not the 0.011–0.018 a naive pool suggests. '6개 paired 차이' is also ambiguous (3 matched pairs aug_i/ctrl_i, 6 checkpoints, or 9 cross pairs), so the rule cannot be applied unambiguously.
fix: Define the unit as the trial: for each of the 640 trials average the failure indicator over the 3 aug and the 3 ctrl attempts, then run one paired test on 640 units (sign/Wilcoxon on the per-trial difference, or a permutation test that flips the aug/ctrl label within trial). Keep the '2 of 3 attempts lower' as a secondary sign check. State the MDD (≈13–20 blocks) so a null result is interpretable.

verdict.reason:
Verified against the document and code; the defect is concrete on both counts.

(1) "6개 paired 차이" is undefined. §3.1 A1 1단계 (NEXT_EXPERIMENTS.md:99) specifies {aug, ctrl} × attempt 1·2·3 evaluated at ONE dev point (C2 −3 dB, n=640). That yields 3 matched pairs (aug_i vs ctrl_i), not 6. Nothing in §3.1, §4 or §5 says what the 6 differences are; the only way to get 6 from the doc is to guess (3 attempts × {best,last} ckpt as in §2.5, or a cross-pairing). Each reading gives different discordant counts and a different p, so the conjunctive rule "…and pooled McNemar p < 0.05", which gates the 10 h N=1.6e5 stage-2 run and the single test-set confirmation, cannot be computed as written. For a pre-registration whose §0 header forbids changing decision rules after commit, that is unfollowable, not a style issue.

(2) The pooling is statistically unsound in the house framework. common.trial_rng(testbed, prior, Nr, T, Tp, snr) (common.py:165) depends only on the cell/SNR, and attempt only changes the training generator (score.py:882), so all six checkpoints are scored on the identical 640 (H, u, perm, noise) realisations. The house paired test (Demo/exp_0921_analysis.py:44-51) is the exact sign test on discordant pairs, whose n is the trial count (the doc itself uses "n=640, 26 블록 이상" for H0). Pooling per-attempt discordant pairs treats them as independent, but the discordance direction on a given trial is shared across attempts whenever the aug-vs-ctrl effect is trial-dependent, so the pooled variance is understated and the p anti-conservative. Quantified with the house sign_p: at discordance 3–8% the n=640 MDD is 11–15 blocks (0.017–0.023 BLER), whereas a naive 3× pool passes at 5.7–9 blocks per attempt (0.009–0.014); the claim's figures are the same order. Minor nuance: concordant "always-fail" blocks do not enter McNemar, so the inflation comes from correlated discordant directions, not from hard blocks; the conclusion is unchanged. Consequence: a false pass into stage 2 and the test-set confirmation is materially more likely than the nominal 5%, and a null cannot be interpreted without an MDD stated at the true n=640.

The proposed fix (aggregate per trial, one paired test on 640 units, keep "2 of 3 attempts" as secondary, state the MDD) resolves both points.

quote: 개선이 유지되면 **테스트 집합 확증 1회**(C2 전 SNR, n=2560, 새 태그, 기존 표 무수정).
title: Test-set confirmation has no decision rule: no primary point, metric, or test across 7 SNRs
consequence: '개선이 유지되면' (dev, 3 points) and 'confirmed' (test, 7 SNRs) are never defined: any of 7 SNRs, BLER or NMSE, any-vs-all points, any p-threshold can be chosen after seeing the test table, and §7 makes this run the trigger for replacing the headline table. This violates the house style the document itself cites (10_SPEC §3c 확증 실행 규칙: named 1차 비교, 양측 부호검정 + 3점 규칙, 판정점 사전 결정, 사후 변경 없음) and 01_RULES §5 ('설정은 실행 전에 확정').
fix: Fix before running: (i) dev gate = C2 −3 dB paired test p < 0.05 with Δ ≤ −MDD, the other two dev points report-only; (ii) test confirmation = one pre-named comparison (aug-V1 vs ctrl-V1, BLER@16, C2 −3/0/+3 dB as the 3 판정점 per 10_SPEC), two-sided sign test + 3점 규칙, other SNRs report-only; (iii) 'headline replaced' only if (ii) passes. Write these lines into §2.6/§3.1 now.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed. NEXT_EXPERIMENTS.md line 100 (§3.1 2단계) reads "개발 집합 3점(C2 −3/+6, C5 −3)에서 V1 wiring paired 비교. 개선이 유지되면 **테스트 집합 확증 1회**(C2 전 SNR, n=2560, 새 태그, 기존 표 무수정)." and line 145 (§7) reads "헤드라인 교체는 테스트 집합 확증 1회 뒤, 새 표로만." Neither "개선이 유지되면" (3 dev points: all? any? which test?) nor what the 7-SNR test run must show for the headline to be replaced is defined anywhere in the document (the only other mentions are line 16 "테스트 BLER 을 보고 무엇도 고르지 않는다" and line 118 "확증에서만 테스트 집합"). By contrast, stage 1 (line 99) is fully specified ("3 attempt 중 2 이상 … 6개 paired 차이를 합친 McNemar p < 0.05"), so this is an omission, not a stylistic choice.

Why it is concrete, not taste: (1) The project's automatic decision machinery does not cover this comparison. analysis.py pair_list() computes the anchored 3-point sign test only for the fixed list (REF→STAGEC_ARMS, M-ours-bstar→STAGEC_ARMS, STAGEC_ARMS→R5-genie), and runner.py:352-353 builds V0/V1/V4 from a single --stagec-ckpt per run, so aug-V1 and ctrl-V1 are both named M-ours-dscore-C-V1 in different tags and can never appear as a pair in one table. The H3 comparison (aug-V1 vs ctrl-V1) therefore has no pre-registered pair, anchor, decision points, or test; the new table will only auto-print bstar→aug-V1, which re-tests the existing headline (already significant) rather than the augmentation hypothesis. (2) Consequence at judgment time: after the test table exists, whether the headline is replaced — and on which of 7 SNRs / which metric / which threshold the "confirmation" is read — is decided post hoc, which conflicts with 01_RULES §5 ("설정은 실행 전에 확정하고, 실행 후에는 바꾸지 않는다") and with the document's own line 16. It also violates the confirmation house style the document says applies ("기존 규칙 … 그대로 적용된다", line 4): 10_SPEC §3c/§6b/§6d/§6g and 08_SPEC §2 all require named 1차 비교, 3 pre-decided 판정점 anchored on the baseline arm, two-sided sign test + power guard, 사후 변경 없음. (3) Handoff §13 requires NEXT_EXPERIMENTS.md to state "선택 기준"; the stage-2→test trigger has none.

Minor inaccuracy in the claim that does not change the verdict: the document cites 10_SPEC §3d·§7, not §3c explicitly; the house-style requirement still applies via line 4 and the project-wide 08_SPEC §2 rule. The proposed fix (name the primary comparison aug-V1 vs ctrl-V1, fix dev gate at C2 −3 dB, fix 3 test 판정점 with the standard sign test + 3점 규칙, and make headline replacement conditional on that pass) is the right shape and must be written before the stage-2 run.

quote: 같은 스트림의 **skip 2560 ~ 3199** (n=640). 어떤 raw 디렉터리에도 쓰인 적 없음(최대 skip 2520). 이 문서의 진단·ablation·선택은 **전부 개발 집합**에서 한다
title: No tool can produce the dev set; the runner always regenerates trials 0..n−1 (the test set)
consequence: runner.py builds tasks with `for s in range(0, a.n, a.chunk)` and exposes no skip offset, so any `runner.py run --n 640 --tag review_next` (the natural way to get the paired V1/mean/ctrl arms of §3.1/§3.2, which are wired through build_our_arms) silently evaluates test trials 0–639 and writes files named skip0…skip600 that look like a dev run. The split is verified disjoint in principle (every trial_rng consumer stays below 2560: sigma.py 64, diag_* ≤128, stratify_L 2560, bench 25), but the document names no mechanism that enforces it, so the leakage it is designed to prevent is the default outcome.
fix: Add to §0: dev runs use a new opt-in runner argument (e.g. --skip0 2560) or a wrapper that passes skip=2560+k·40 to build_point, and the acceptance check that every dev raw filename carries skip ≥ 2560 (fail otherwise). Until that code exists, mark §3.1/§3.2 BLER rows as 'not runnable'.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. runner.py:487-488 builds run tasks as `for s in range(0, a.n, a.chunk)` and the argparser (runner.py:1015-1047) exposes no skip/offset flag (--seed is refused), so `runner.py run --n 640 --tag <x>` re-evaluates test trials 0-639 and writes files named skip0..skip600 that look like a dev run. The document (NEXT_EXPERIMENTS.md:15, 77, 99-100, 106-108, 118) makes dev-set (skip 2560-3199) paired BLER the primary metric for §2.5/§3.1/§3.2 but names new code only for §2.1-§2.4; §3.2 is wired through build_our_arms(mean_arms=True) (arms.py:140 -> runner.build_point), so the runner is the implied and only paired-arm BLER tool. §0 defines test membership by the raw filename skip field yet sets no acceptance check that dev files carry skip >= 2560. Every existing trial_rng consumer starts at trial 0 and all raw dirs top out at skip2520, so the split is disjoint in principle but unenforced in practice: the default path silently selects on the test set, voiding the one-shot confirmation run (01_RULES §5). Fix is small (task builder `range(a.skip0, a.skip0 + a.n, a.chunk)`; run_task already handles arbitrary skip) plus the filename acceptance check; until then §2.5/§3.1/§3.2 BLER rows are not runnable as written.

title: C2 +6 dB at n=640 has zero power for any BLER or AUC decision
consequence: On the test set V1 BLER at +6 dB is 0.0063 (16 failures in 2560) and V1-vs-b* discordance is 0.0078; at n=640 that is ≈4 failures and ≈5 discordant pairs. Exact McNemar cannot reach p < 0.05 unless ≥6 discordant pairs all fall one way, the 'AUC ≥ 0.6' failure-prediction statistics of §2.1/§2.4 rest on ~4 positives, and the §3.1 2단계 rule '개선이 유지되면' over 3 points becomes a coin flip at this point (or a forking path if 'any point' is meant).
fix: Either make +6 dB report-only (no decision weight) and state that only C2 −3 dB (and C5 −3 dB if it has ≥50 failures) carries the decision, or raise n at +6 dB to ≥6400 (skip 2560–8959, still disjoint) so ~40 failures exist. Say which in §2.6.

verdict.reason: Confirmed against the raw test-set files (conf/raw_B16e4k, C2 +6 dB, skip 0..2520, n=2560): V1 has 16 failures (0.00625) and V1-vs-b* discordant pairs are 4+16=20 (0.0078), exactly as claimed. Contiguous 640-block quarters of that stream give V1 failures 5/4/3/4 and discordant pairs 9/2/6/3. The comparison the document actually schedules at this point (§3.1 2단계, aug vs ctrl, both under V1 wiring) is same-family; the closest existing proxy V1-vs-V4 differs on only 1+1 blocks in 2560 at +6 dB, so an n=640 run expects ~0-1 discordant pairs. Exact McNemar two-sided p<0.05 needs >=6 pairs all one way; the AUC>=0.6 threshold of §2.6 (C-pseudo, C-cavity) and the H1/H4 rejection conditions, evaluated with ~4 positives, is crossed ~25% of the time under the null (Hanley-McNeil SE ~0.145) versus ~0.1% at -3 dB. The document does hang decisions on this point: '개발 집합 3점(C2 −3/+6, C5 −3)에서 V1 wiring paired 비교. 개선이 유지되면 테스트 집합 확증 1회' states no aggregation rule, and per-point judgement is what the handoff (§7 P1-1 'Iteration, C1/C2/C5, SNR별로 분리한다') and the document's own §7 prediction ('C-cavity 는 C5 에서만 만족') imply. So when results arrive, the go/no-go to test confirmation and the C-pseudo/H4 verdict at +6 dB will be decided by 0-4 events with no pre-stated rule, which is the forking path 01_RULES §5 forbids. n=640 itself breaks no rule (it is the §9.6 floor), and the point is legitimately included for σ≈0.10 coverage of the median/IQR cavity metrics; the defect is confined to failure-count statistics (paired BLER go/no-go, AUC) and is a concrete power/aggregation gap, not taste. Severity medium is fair; the report-only fix (decision weight on C2 −3 dB only, stated in §2.6) is the minimal correction.

quote: 임계값 근거: 0.10 은 감사의 예비 측정(n=16, 미저장: 0.29/0.16/0.07)이 하·중 구간에서 넘고 상 구간에서 못 넘는 값으로, 예비 측정을 확인하는 검사가 된다.
title: C-phase threshold was set between already-observed values on a subset of its own test sample
consequence: The audit's 0.29/0.16/0.07 were measured on the first 64 samples of train_rng stream 10 (REVIEW_AUDIT P1-3a 방법), which are the first 64 of the n=512 stream-10 sample §2.3 will use; 0.10 was then placed between 0.16 and 0.07. The condition is therefore a replication of a value already seen, not a gate: it cannot fail, and §7 records the outcome in advance. It nonetheless authorises ≈10 GPU-hours (A1 2단계), so the document's claim that ablations run only when a diagnostic '만족' is decorative for A1.
fix: Either declare A1 unconditional given the audit and drop C-phase, or make it a real test: evaluate §2.3 on an independent stream (train_rng which=11, as diag_h4_psd_indep already does) and set the threshold by a cost-relevant criterion fixed before looking (e.g. ε_φ/denoising error ≥ the V1-vs-GMM GB′ gap on the same band), not by bracketing the preliminary numbers.

verdict.reason: Premise is factually wrong: the audit's pilot (chk_p13_p14.py) drew sample_vecs(train_rng(...,10), 64); D2Gen._draw (d2.py:134-140) is vectorized over n, so a 64-draw is not a prefix of the 512-draw §2.3 will use — CPU check shows 0 shared rows. No leakage exists, and the 'use stream 11' fix would change nothing. The pilot ratios were also independently reproduced on 48 fresh samples (rng 12345; REVIEW_AUDIT.md:473), so the threshold sitting below them reflects the checkpoint, not the sample. No rule conflict: 01_RULES §5 forbids BLER-driven choices, not pilot-informed thresholds, and 10_SPEC_stageC §3c explicitly endorses post-hoc-registered conditions grounded in pre-measured evidence; the document itself declares C-phase a confirmation check and §7 predicts it. Consequence is misattributed: C-phase gates only A1 1단계 (≈1.5 GPU-h); the ≈10 GPU-h 2단계 is gated by 1단계's own falsifiable rule (2/3 attempts + McNemar p<0.05). Remaining point (weak gate) is design taste. Minor unrelated slip: doc says n=16 but P1-3a used n=64.

quote: C-clip | §2.2 에서 실제 질의의 site 전후 평균 이동 중앙값 ≥ 0.02 (반복 ≥ 4) **또는** clip 비율 ≥ 10%
title: C-clip is already decided by test-set data; the OR clause cannot fail
consequence: The V1 site-clip fraction on the headline test raw (raw_B16e4k, all 448 files) is 0.69–0.91 at every SNR and b* is 0.46–0.80 (REVIEW_AUDIT P1-4b), so 'clip 비율 ≥ 10%' is known to hold before any dev run; the mean-shift clause (median 4e-5–1.3e-3 on the same record) is known to fail. A2 is thus unconditional, the threshold was chosen after seeing test-set statistics, and H5 itself was generated from the test raw that the §7 confirmation would later reuse. Presenting this as a progression condition misstates the design.
fix: Drop the clip-rate clause (or restate it as 'known: 69–91% on B16e4k, A2 runs unconditionally') and keep only the mean-shift clause if a gate is wanted. Add a sentence that H5/A2 hypotheses were formed from test-set clip statistics, and if A2 is ever to be confirmed, use a fresh test stream (skip ≥ 3200) rather than the already-analysed 0–2559.

verdict.reason:
Core of the claim verified; two of its supporting assertions are wrong, but the defect stands on its own.

VERIFIED (recomputed from all 448 files in /home/HTJ/t2/conf/raw_B16e4k, key '<arm>|clip' = (n_clip/n_site, shift/n_clip) per trial, runner.py:417): M-ours-dscore-C-V1 clip fraction mean 0.908/0.869/0.826/0.767/0.725/0.702/0.689 at -3..15 dB (n=2560 per SNR, per-trial p05 >= 0.06 at -3..3 dB); M-ours-bstar 0.798..0.459. The pre-reg's dev set (line 15: same `common.trial_rng` stream, skip 2560-3199) is iid from the same stream, so a dev-set "clip 비율 ≥ 10%" is a certain pass. With the OR, line 85 "C-clip | ... 평균 이동 중앙값 ≥ 0.02 (반복 ≥ 4) **또는** clip 비율 ≥ 10%" cannot fail, and A2 is unconditional.

Why this is a soundness defect, not taste:
1. Line 41 "H3·H5 의 ablation 은 H1~H4 의 진단이 §2.6 의 진행 조건을 만족할 때만 실행한다" is substantively false for H5: the decisive input already exists in the doc's own cited evidence (REVIEW_AUDIT P1-4b/P2-Ca, listed as 근거 at line 3).
2. The "임계값 근거" paragraph (line 91) gives provenance for 0.10, 0.2/AUC 0.6, [0.7,1.4], [0.8,1.25] and says which were set "예비 자료 없이" — but omits 10% and 0.02, the only thresholds whose outcome was already known from n=2560x7 data. The doc claims 10_SPEC §7 house style applies (line 3), and that house style requires disclosing already-seen provenance (10_SPEC §3c "출처 (숨기지 않는다)", §6f "예측을 적기 전의 공개 (중요)", §6h "데이터는 이미 있고 아직 읽지 않았다"). Not disclosed here.
3. Concrete consequence when results are judged: the "불만족 시 → H5 는 실행하지 않고 '이동 작음' 으로 기록" branch is unreachable. If the dev-set mean shift comes in below 0.02 (the doc's own pre-registered "small" threshold, i.e. the direct measurement of H5's claimed mechanism "clip 이 belief 평균을 이동시키는 것"), A2 still runs and H5 (line 39) is judged solely on A2 BLER — H5 can be reported "supported" while its mechanism was measured below the registered threshold, and the doc has no rule for that case.
4. Additional undisclosed test-stream origin: the only mean-vs-eta BLER evidence behind H5 (settling_D2.txt, n=256, V0/N=1e4: dscore|mean 0.184 vs eta 0.824 at -3 dB) was produced by conf/code/diag_psd_cf.py:114 calling C.trial_rng(...) with no skip, i.e. trials 0-255 of the same stream as test skip 0-2559. NEXT_EXPERIMENTS.md never mentions settling/skip-0 origin (grep: only line 14).

CORRECTIONS to the claim (do not rescue the gate, but should be fixed in the finding):
(a) "the mean-shift clause is known to fail" is NOT established. The raw shift is sum |mu-hH|^2/|hH|^2 per clipped call under the isotropic cavity (t2_gmm.py:119), a SQUARED ratio; sqrt of the medians is 0.032 (-3 dB), 0.034 (0 dB), 0.021 (+6 dB), 0.004 (15 dB) — straddling 0.02. And the doc's §2.2 quantity ‖h_post − h_H‖/‖h_H‖ (colored posterior vs denoiser mean, cf. §3.2 M3 caveat) is a different, unmeasured quantity. quote: C-cavity | §2.1 에서 e_t 중앙값 ∉ [0.7, 1.4] (반복 ≥ 4) **또는** C5 에서 cond(G) 중앙값 > 100 인 반복에 score 질의가 있음 | P2-B(공분산 조건부 denoiser) 프로토타입 설계 문서

quote: 개발 집합에서 ν-보정비 e_t (§2.1) 중앙값이 반복 4 이상에서 [0.7, 1.4] 안이고, 실패/성공 블록 간 e_t 분포 차이가 없다 (AUC < 0.6)
title: H1 rejection requires AUC < 0.6 on a statistic whose numerator is the channel error, so H1 is effectively unfalsifiable
consequence: e_t = ‖q − h_true‖²/(N ν_q) contains the receiver's own channel-estimate error. Any block that fails because the channel estimate is wrong (at C2 −3 dB V1 BLER 0.145 vs genie 0.034, i.e. ~75% of V1 failures are channel-related) has a large e_t at iteration 8 by definition, so AUC ≥ 0.6 is essentially certain regardless of whether the cavity's variance ν_q is mis-calibrated. Because rejection needs BOTH clauses (AND), the AUC clause alone keeps H1 from ever being rejected, and the write-up will report 'deviation concentrates in failed blocks' as a finding when it is a tautology (failure ⇔ large error).
fix: Make the rejection an OR of the two clauses, or replace the AUC clause with one that separates cavity mis-calibration from plain estimation error: e.g. compare e_t only within blocks that R5-genie also decodes (channel-driven failures), or test whether e_t at iteration 4 predicts failure beyond the block's NMSE at iteration 4 (partial AUC / logistic with NMSE as covariate), or compare against the ρ_tr of §2.2 which normalises by the denoiser's predicted variance.

verdict.reason:
Verdict: the defect is real (H1's rejection clause is unsatisfiable in practice), but the claim's stated mechanism is wrong and should be corrected before it is acted on.

Document line (NEXT_EXPERIMENTS.md:35): "개발 집합에서 ν-보정비 e_t (§2.1) 중앙값이 반복 4 이상에서 [0.7, 1.4] 안이고, 실패/성공 블록 간 e_t 분포 차이가 없다 (AUC < 0.6)" — rejection is the AND of both clauses, and §2.1 (line 52) fixes the AUC as "반복 8 의 e_t 로 최종 실패 예측".

What the claim gets wrong: e_t is NOT "large by definition" in failed blocks. In the V1 wiring (arms.py MODULE_H["score"]: mode=scalar, scal=belief) ν_q = aL/(1−aL)·ν_E (t2_route_a.py:364) is set by the decoder's posterior variances and the denoiser's α_H, so the ratio only blows up if ν_q fails to track the error. In a CPU control run I did (perfectly matched Kron-Gaussian truth + the same Gaussian prior as Module H, exact closed-form denoiser, V1 loop config from arms.LOOP/MODULE_H["score"], C2 geometry 8x4 T=16 Tp=4, private RNG, n=250 per SNR; script at /tmp/claude-1005/-home-HTJ-t2-Demo/d3790660-21e8-42b4-971e-49b4049a6e64/scratchpad/et_auc_check.py), the iteration-8 e_t median was 1.10 overall, 1.01 in successful blocks and 1.28 in failed blocks at −3 dB (99 fails), and 1.01 / 1.00 / 1.24 at 0 dB (13 fails). Failed blocks are inside the document's own "calibrated" band [0.7, 1.4], so the numerator-driven "large e_t" story is false.

What makes the defect real anyway: even in that exact-prior null model — where the training assumption q = h + CN(0, ν_q I) is satisfied by construction and the D-14 site is exact (no clip) — the AUC(e_t@8 → fail@16) was 0.82 at −3 dB and 0.75 at 0 dB (0.82/0.72 already at n=20). AUC is a rank statistic with no effect-size floor; the EP loop's small, universal overconfidence in decoder-failed blocks (median 1.0 → 1.28) is enough to push it far above 0.6, and with the pre-registered n=640 (~93 failures at C2 −3 dB, SE ≈ 0.03) the clause will fail decisively. Since rejection requires BOTH clauses, H1 cannot be rejected even when the prior is exact and every stratum's median is inside the band. Consequence when results are judged against the document: at C2, where §7 predicts C-cavity does not fire (median in band), H1 will be reported as "not rejected — 이탈이 실패 블록에 집중" for V1, although a matched-Gaussian control gives the same AUC; the document's stated goal (line 5: separate prior / adapter / loop) is defeated for H1, and §2.1's arm list (M-ours-bstar, V1, V0) contains no scalar-wiring control against which the V1 AUC could be compared (bstar runs in mode="colored"/ep_site and never forms a (q, ν_q) at all). Confirmed supporting number: V1 0.145 vs R5-genie 0.034 at C2 −3 dB (tables_D2_B16e4k.txt:71,75).

Scope note: no §2.6 progression rule uses the H1 AUC (C-cavity keys on the median and cond(G)), so the defect corrupts the pre-registered H1 verdict and its write-up, not the P2-B decision. Sound fixes: make rejection an OR of the two clauses; or give the AUC clause an effect-size requirement (e.g. failed-block median e_t outside [0.7, 1.4], or AUC exceeding that of a matched-Gaussian/loop control arm run in the same scalar wiring on the same dev trials). The claim's proposed "restrict to blocks R5-genie decodes" would not help; the NMSE-covariate partial AUC would, but it tests a different statement than the one H1 makes.

(3) Pair unspecified: §2.5 L77 compares three weight sets {기존 last-EMA, 재학습 last, 재학습 best} → three pairwise Δ; H0 L34 never names which one decides. H0's parenthetical "(val 상대차 6.3e-5)" refers to the legacy run's best@1764 vs last@1784 (REVIEW_AUDIT L63), whose best weights are BEST_WEIGHTS_UNAVAILABLE, so H0 as literally written is untestable; 기존 last-EMA vs 재학습 (any) folds in GPU run-to-run nondeterminism, which §2.5 L76 explicitly allows ("bit-identical 일 것을 요구하지 않는다"). Consequence: H0 is the decision on whether the legacy last-EMA headline stands (L26, L145), and with a 4× ambiguous threshold and an unnamed pair it can be declared either way from identical results, violating the document's own L3 commitment that rules are fixed before observation. Not a style matter; the fix in the claim (one threshold written once, pair = 재학습 best vs 재학습 last, 기존-vs-재학습 reported as nondeterminism reference) is the minimal correction. Minor nuance: the claim's "roughly a third" is slightly high (0.14–0.26 at measured discordance), but that does not change the verdict.

quote: 판정: V1-mean 이 V1-eta 대비 개선이고 GMM-mean 의 개선폭이 그보다 작으면 "adapter 이득이 prior 에 특이적" — 아니면 adapter 일반 효과.

quote: **또는** C5 에서 cond(G) 중앙값 > 100 인 반복에 score 질의가 있음
title: The C5 clause of C-cavity is satisfied by construction, so the P2-B trigger is unconditional
consequence: At C5 (Tp=3 < Nt=4) G at iteration 1 is pilot-only and rank-deficient on every block (10_SPEC §6j: Nr(Nt−Tp) null directions; the document itself says 'G 가 초기에 특이'), so cond(G) = ∞ > 100, and the score arm always queries at iteration 1. The condition holds before any measurement; §7's 'C-cavity 는 C5 에서만 만족' is a tautology, not a prediction, and the pre-registered gate to the P2-B design has no discriminating power.
fix: Condition on what the denoiser actually receives: anisotropy a_t of the regularised cavity SigL = (I/ν_E + G)^{-1} or e_t at iterations ≥ 2, with a threshold; or delete the clause and keep only the e_t ∉ [0.7, 1.4] clause.

verdict.reason: Confirmed against code. In Demo/t2_route_a.py:339-345 the data-column sites are zero at t=0 (rD=0, lh_form="A"), so G at iteration 1 is pilot-only and identical for every block; with Nt=4, Nr=8, Tp=3 a CPU check gives exactly 8 zero eigenvalues (min ~ -1e-15, max 2.0), so cond(G)=λ_max/λ_min is infinite/undefined and the per-block median is >100 by construction (even the guard-G-1 regularised G+I/1e4 gives ~2e4). The V1/V0 score arms (conf/code/arms.py:37: scal="belief", init_colored=0, nu_sw=None) call prior.denoise at t=0, so a score query at that iteration is guaranteed. Hence the clause "C5 에서 cond(G) 중앙값 > 100 인 반복에 score 질의가 있음" is true before any data, the "불만족 시 P2-B 보류" branch of §2.6 is unreachable, and the §7 prediction "C-cavity 는 C5 에서만 만족" has no miss path (violating the spec's own §6j "빗나갈 경로" house style). Concretely, H1 can be rejected on its own criterion (e_t within [0.7,1.4], AUC<0.6) while C-cavity is still recorded as satisfied and P2-B design proceeds, which misrepresents a design constant as a diagnostic finding. The quantity the denoiser actually sees, SigL=(I/ν_E+G)^{-1}, has eigenvalue ratio only 1+Nt/σ²=3 at −3 dB, so cond(G) also does not measure the anisotropy the clause is meant to detect; the document's own a_t metric (or the e_t clause alone) is the sound gate.

The same numbers are in the doc's cited 근거 (REVIEW_AUDIT.md P1-4b line 523/527 "0.908 / 0.869 / … / 0.689"; P2-Ca line 547 "clip fires in 69-91% of V1 site calls"). title: Tier definitions disagree at grid point 15, and the '상' tier excluded from C-phase/C-calib is inside the receiver's real query range
consequence: sigma_grid_D2.txt is 0-indexed k=0..19. Read 1-indexed, point 15 = k=14 has σ=0.3602 ≤ 0.40 (중 by σ, 상 by index); read 0-indexed, point 7 = k=7 has σ=0.109 > 0.10. Tier membership — and hence the C-phase median — shifts by one grid point depending on the reading. Worse, the same file gives C2 −3 dB it1 ν_q=0.4988 → σ=0.499 and it2 σ=0.357, C5 −3 dB it1 σ≈0.71: the judgment-SNR early-iteration queries are in the 상 tier that C-phase ('하·중 구간 중 하나 이상') and C-calib ('하·중 구간 격자점의 1/3') exclude. §6p argues those first queries are where the prior matters most, so the conditions can fail to fire on a defect present in the receiver's actual range.
fix: Define tiers by 0-indexed k and σ consistently (e.g. 하 k=0–6 σ≤0.092, 중 k=7–14 σ≤0.360, 상 k=15–19) and either include 상 in the C-phase/C-calib scope or scope them to the per-iteration query range that §2.1 measures, not the it16 median.

verdict.reason:
Core defect CONFIRMED; two supporting details in the claim are unsupported.

Verified (NEXT_EXPERIMENTS.md:18 vs conf/results/sigma_grid_D2.txt, k=0..19):
- 1-indexed reading: 하 = k0–6 (σ 0.033–0.092, ≤0.10 OK), 중 = k7–13 (0.109–0.304 OK), 상 = k14–19 — but k14 has σ=0.3602 ≤ 0.40, so it is 중 by the σ rule and 상 by the index rule. 0-indexed reading is worse: k7 (σ=0.109) violates "σ ≤ 0.10" and "15~20" needs a nonexistent k=20. No reading makes line 18 self-consistent; membership of k=14 is genuinely undetermined.
- That point is not a corner: C2 −3 dB it2 ν_q=0.2551 → σ=0.357 and C2 0 dB it1 ν_q=0.25 → σ=0.354 land exactly there.
- Decision relevance: C-calib (line 88) counts "하·중 구간 격자점의 1/3 이상" — 14 points (index) vs 15 (σ); threshold is 5 either way, so a run with 4 failing points in k0–13 plus a failing k14 fires under the σ reading and not under the index reading. H2's kill condition (line 36, "2/3 이상") has the same 9-vs-10 edge. A judge can choose the reading post hoc, which is what the pre-registration is supposed to preclude.
- §0's "수신기가 C2 에서 실제 질의하는 범위는 … (하·중 구간)" misstates the cited file: C2 −3 dB it1 ν_q=0.4988 → σ=0.499 (상), and the pooled p90 of the same file is σ=0.499. The judgment-SNR first query is outside the tier that H2/C-calib are scoped to.

Not supported in the claim: (1) there is no "§6p" in NEXT_EXPERIMENTS.md or the handoff (headings are §0–§8, P0-x/P1-x/P2-x); (2) no sigma_grid file has C5 per-iteration ν_q (only C1, C2, C6), so "C5 −3 dB it1 σ≈0.71" is not from "the same file"; (3) C-phase is unaffected in practice — it fires on 하 alone (prelim 0.27–0.29 from REVIEW_AUDIT.md:473) and the prelim 상 value 0.07 < 0.10, so including 상 would not change it; C-calib's consequence is report-only. Practical severity is low–medium (bites H2 verdict and C-calib in edge cases), but the self-contradiction at k=14 and the misstatement of the query range are concrete, not taste. Fix as proposed: define tiers by k (e.g. 하 k0–6, 중 k7–14, 상 k15–19) with matching σ bounds, and either include 상 in H2/C-calib or state explicitly that it1–it2 queries at ≤0 dB are out of scope.

quote: 지표: GB′(held-out denoising NMSE, GMM b\*=kron K=512@1e4 대비), ε_φ, **개발 집합 C2 −3 dB n=640 BLER (V1 wiring)**. 판정: 3 attempt 중 2 이상에서 aug 의 개발 BLER 이 ctrl 보다 낮고, 6개 paired 차이를 합친 McNemar p < 0.05.
title: Which checkpoint (best or last) the aug/ctrl arms load is unspecified, and the pooled McNemar is ill-defined
consequence: Post-P0 score.train writes both <ckpt> (last) and <ckpt>_best.pt; the document never says which one A1 evaluates, leaving a free choice after results are seen (and §2.5's H0 outcome could be used post hoc to justify either). '6개 paired 차이' is undefined — three attempts give three aug-vs-ctrl pairs — and pooling across attempts over the same 640 trials treats correlated block outcomes as independent, making p anti-conservative. Two undisclosed degrees of freedom sit in the rule that gates the 10 h stage-2 run.
fix: Write '모든 신규 학습 arm 은 `_best.pt` 로 평가 (legacy V1 만 last-EMA)' (or bind the rule to one role and report the other). Replace the pooled test with per-attempt paired sign/McNemar tests plus the 2-of-3 majority rule, or a block-level test stratified by attempt.

verdict.reason:
Both halves of the claim check out against the document and code.

(1) Checkpoint role is genuinely unspecified and is a free run-time choice. conf/code/score.py train() (L834-836, L991-996) now writes `<ckpt>` with role='last' and `<ckpt>_best.pt` with role='best'; evaluation loads exactly the path the operator passes (`score.load_prior(ckpt=...)` = "caller override", runner `--stagec-ckpt` L1076-1084), with no preference for either file — runner.py L151 merely annotates "evaluated = LAST epoch; the best-epoch weights are in the _best.pt sibling". NEXT_EXPERIMENTS.md §3.1 A1 says only "개발 집합 C2 −3 dB n=640 BLER (V1 wiring)" for stage 1 and "통제군 = §2.5 재학습" for stage 2; §2.5 produces both files and explicitly evaluates {기존 last-EMA, 재학습 last, 재학습 best}, so the document itself treats best-vs-last as open (H0) rather than settled by convention. H0 is tested only at N=1.6e5, while A1 stage 1 trains 6 arms at N=1e4, where REVIEW_AUDIT P0-1b gives the EMA gap as 0.999^720 ≈ 0.49 (vs 1.3e-5 at 1.6e5) — a materially different regime, so an H0 outcome cannot be used to settle the stage-1 choice either. With 6 arms and 2 candidate files each, the "3 attempt 중 2 이상" majority can be flipped after results are seen.

(2) "6개 paired 차이를 합친 McNemar p < 0.05" is not computable as written. Stage 1 has {aug, ctrl} × 3 attempts = 6 arms on the same dev trials (skip 2560–3199, paired by §0); aug_i vs ctrl_i yields 3 paired differences, all-pairs would be 9, nothing yields 6. The house precedent (conf/code/analysis.py table_B, PAPER_MATERIALS "pooled a:b") pools discordant pairs across distinct SNR points that have distinct trial streams; pooling across attempts here reuses the identical 640 realisations three times, so discordant outcomes on a block are correlated across seeds and the pooled McNemar/sign p treats 3×640 as independent — anti-conservative in the direction that passes the gate.

Consequence: this rule is the sole gate for the ≈10 h stage-2 run and the one-shot test-set confirmation (§3.1 2단계). As written it leaves the file choice open (post-hoc degree of freedom) and its p-value criterion has no defined computation, so results cannot be judged against the document unambiguously. Not a style matter.

quote: 기존 레시피·seed·split 그대로 `d2sx_N160000_a1` 을 **새 태그**(`ckpt_review_next/ctrl_N160000_a1.pt`)로 재학습 … 예산: 같은 GPU 1개, ≈10 h
title: Retraining a pre-registered run is scheduled without the approval/DECISIONS marker the rules require
consequence: 01_RULES §5: '재실행이 필요해 보이면 그 이유를 DECISIONS에 적고 사용자 판단으로 남긴다'; CLAUDE.md: 장시간 학습은 실행 전 사용자 승인. CHANGELOG_REVIEW §5 records this exact retrain as '별도 승인' pending, but §2.5 and the §6 status row present it as an unconditional design step. Without the marker, the record cannot show the rerun was authorised rather than opportunistic.
fix: Add '사용자 승인 + DECISIONS 1행 후 실행' to §2.5 and to the §6 row (also for A1 stage 2, another 10 h run).

verdict.reason:
Not a concrete defect of the pre-registration; it is an administrative reminder that would not change how results are judged against the document.

(1) The rule cited (01_RULES §5:78) prohibits re-running a pre-registered run because results disappointed ("결과가 기대와 다르게 나와도 재실행하지 않는다 … 재실행이 필요해 보이면 그 이유를 DECISIONS에 적고 사용자 판단으로 남긴다"). §2.5 is not that: it is a NEW-tag control run (`ckpt_review_next/ctrl_N160000_a1.pt`) whose sole purpose is to obtain the `_best.pt` the P0 fix now saves, with the original `ckpt/d2sx_*` read-only (§0 "결과 보존"), the headline unchanged (§7 bullet 1), and a pre-stated prediction "H0 채택(|Δ| < 0.01)". That is exactly what the handoff (basis document, line 260) prescribes: "이를 수정한 재학습은 별도 tag로 실행하며 과거 결과를 덮어쓰지 않는다." The "reason" the rule wants written down IS written down, in the pre-registration itself (§2.5, three bullets), before any result is seen — a stronger form of non-opportunism than a DECISIONS one-liner.

(2) "사용자 승인" (CLAUDE.md) and "사용자 판단" (01_RULES) bind execution, not document text. NEXT_EXPERIMENTS never claims the run may proceed without approval; §6 lists it as 미실행, line 4 states "기존 규칙(01_RULES.md §5 …)은 그대로 적용된다" (incorporating the approval rule by reference), and CHANGELOG_REVIEW §5 — cited as the document's basis — already records this retrain as "GPU·장시간 → 별도 승인". Whether approval was actually obtained is an execution-time record (DECISIONS/STATUS/commit), which can exist regardless of whether §2.5 repeats the sentence.

(3) When results are later judged against §2.5/§3.1, what matters is the tag, dev set (skip 2560–3199, n=640), paired comparison, metrics, and the |Δ|<0.01 prediction — none of which depend on an approval marker. Running without approval would be a process violation independent of the document's wording; adding "사용자 승인 + DECISIONS 1행 후 실행" is a stylistic/administrative annotation (the claim itself rates it "low"), which the harness's default classifies as real=false.

quote: (a) 등변 오차 / denoising 오차 중앙값이 세 구간 모두 < 0.10 → augmentation 자체를 하지 않는다.

consequence: H3(a) rejects only if all three tiers are < 0.10; C-phase fires only if 하 or 중 is ≥ 0.10 and otherwise says 'H3 기각(a)'. If only 상 ≥ 0.10, H3 is not rejected by (a) yet C-phase records it as rejected. The rule cannot be followed in that case.

quote: {aug, ctrl} × attempt 1·2·3 (attempt = 학습 seed)
title: Attempts share the initial weights, so '2 of 3 attempts' is weaker seed-robustness than stated
consequence: CHANGELOG_REVIEW §5 (user decision 2026-09-23, not fixed): make_model draws from the torch global RNG without an explicit seed, so in the one-process wrappers every attempt starts from the same init; attempt only changes the data/noise generator (score.py:882). The majority rule then measures batch-order variation, not initialisation variation, and the document presents it as seed robustness.
fix: State this limitation in §3.1, or seed init from attempt only in the new opt-in phase_aug path (keeping the default stream bit-identical, which the selftest already checks).

verdict.reason: The claimed mechanism is factually wrong. The claim asserts that in the one-process-per-run wrappers "every attempt starts from the same init" because make_model draws from the unseeded torch global RNG. But PyTorch does not seed the default CPU generator with a fixed value per process: `torch.initial_seed()` in two fresh `~/miniforge3/envs/torch/bin/python` processes returned 8034024878902116645 and 15716516201007763051. Building `score.make_model("D2SXNR1610000", HP, 16, 4)` with the exact train_nr16.py HP in two fresh processes gave different weight hashes (sha256 0a5147b2… vs c8119245…). Nothing in `score.train` (score.py:825-923), `training_split` (own np default_rng(SEED_SPLIT)), `_val_draws` (own generator SEED_VAL), or the wrappers (train_nr16.py, run_d2_sx.py, common.py, arms.py, sigma.py) calls torch.manual_seed; the only `torch.manual_seed(0)` (score.py:1540) is under `if __name__ == "__main__"` for selftests. So attempts 1/2/3 do NOT share initial weights: each gets an independent random init, and the "2 of 3 attempts" rule therefore does capture initialisation variation (in addition to the attempt-seeded data/noise stream at score.py:882). The stated consequence ("measures batch-order variation, not initialisation variation") does not occur. Note for the reviewer: the actual limitation is the opposite one — init is unseeded and unrecorded, so a single attempt is not bit-reproducible and CHANGELOG_REVIEW §5's rationale "한 프로세스인 현재 wrapper들은 torch 기본 seed로 재현되지만" is itself false. That is a reproducibility/recording issue (§5 "seed 를 결과 파일 헤더에 적는다" would need the init seed to be captured), a different claim from this one, and it does not weaken the majority rule as this claim states.

title: Equal-budget claim for phase augmentation is asserted, not argued
consequence: Fresh random phases every epoch mean the network never sees the same sample twice — a reviewer will read that as more data than the GMM received (01_RULES §5 'diffusion에 GMM보다 많은 데이터·예산을 주지 않는다'). The defensible answer — the zero-mean CN mixture is exactly phase-invariant by construction (audit P1-3a: GMM equivariance error ~1e-15), so augmentation only supplies a symmetry the GMM already has — is nowhere in the document, and the GMM control is not asked to demonstrate it.
fix: Add one sentence with the invariance argument and include the GMM b* ε_φ (~1e-15) from §2.3 as the control row in the A1 table.

verdict.reason: Exposition gap, not a defect that changes how results are judged. (1) No conflict with the rule as written: 01_RULES §5 operationalises equal budget as "동일 N_train=1e4, 동일 분할"; §3.1 A1 keeps the same set, same N_train, same split and only applies a per-sample rotation — it adds no samples, restarts or epoch budget beyond the frozen recipe shared with ctrl. (2) The "never sees the same input twice" objection already applies to every accepted diffusion checkpoint: score.train draws fresh DSM noise e each step (score.py:943), so phase aug introduces no new category of budget concern. (3) The reconciliation is a mathematical identity, not a result-dependent choice: D2 draws per-path psi ~ U[0,2pi) (conf/code/d2.py:139), so the prior is exactly global-phase invariant, and the baseline fits p(h)=sum_k pi_k CN(h;0,C_k) (Demo/t2_gmm.py:6,137) whose EM sufficient statistic h h^H is invariant to e^{j phi} — the GMM fit would be bit-for-bit unchanged by the same augmentation. Stating this later cannot be gamed post hoc and alters no threshold, decision rule or arm comparison. (4) The claim's sub-point that "the GMM control is not asked to demonstrate it" is wrong: NEXT_EXPERIMENTS.md line 65 already requires "GMM b* 대조(기대 ~1e-15)" for eps_phi, and A1's metric list (line 99) includes eps_phi. (5) A1's decision rule (line 99) compares aug vs ctrl, both diffusion with identical code/seeds; the GMM appears only in the stage-2 test-set table, where the aug arm is still same-N_train/same-split. Adding the one-sentence invariance note is a reasonable clarity improvement but is a matter of presentation.
